recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If FM and OO want current R6 core Claim-family request elements to target the external OO Incubator SupplyRequest resource, that should be handled by a current work-group decision rather than by reapplying this R5 Claim issue.
issue_request: FHIR-22659 was Published with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution for Financial Management. It requested support for preauthorization claims to reference requested procedures/services without misusing Procedure, resolved by adding .request 0..* Reference(DeviceRequest | MedicationRequest | NutritionOrder | ServiceRequest | SupplyRequest | VisionPrescription) to Claim.item, ClaimResponse.addItem, ExplanationOfBenefit.item, and ExplanationOfBenefit.addItem.
initial_application: Commit 2be1440043170cc0df19d0f270235e5d232d262d, merged by 03a95e1a21, applied the issue for R5 by adding all four request elements to the Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit StructureDefinition XML files with the full approved target list. Published R5 profile JSON confirms the same four elements and targets.
additional_context: Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit remain active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. Current source and build output still include Claim.item.request, ClaimResponse.addItem.request, ExplanationOfBenefit.item.request, and ExplanationOfBenefit.addItem.request with ServiceRequest as an allowed target. The only approved R5 target absent now is SupplyRequest, which commit 3b38b80cf23f9cbb306fab8fcedb293315478c32 removed from these active core targetProfile lists while removing OO resources from the active core resource list and pointing them to the OO Incubator. Later FHIR-43308 discusses broader future Claim/EOB request and event modeling but is still Triaged and was not decided here.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the seed's ServiceRequest requirement is already present, and re-adding SupplyRequest would reverse a later core/OO resource-boundary change rather than reconcile FHIR-22659.
